review.rationale: The case is otherwise sound: the task is now a read-only 'which channel' question, correctly avoiding the reactions.remove single-reactor-ownership restriction that would have made a state-changing version unsupported. The focal selector follows the assigned route (message_reactions.user_id→users→channel_members) literally, placing the 'named Robert' filter on the USER node per the binding_note's explicit clarification that the reactor's own membership, not the message's channel, is the identifying edge. The two auxiliary queries (Lukas-authorship via messages/users, and engineering-channel-name via channel_members/channels) are properly independent extensions since CHANNELS lies outside the three assigned route nodes, and are not smuggled into the locked identifying path. Both candidate reactions (Walsh on the circuit-tracer OOM message in #engineering; Chen on the OOM/memory-leak root-cause message in #core-infra) are genuine, symmetric, fully-grounded resolutions matching the prompt's stated conditions, correctly instantiated as new seed_edits with valid composite keys. Hubert's negative correctly fails on reactor-name; Morgan's negative correctly fails on reactor-name and message-authorship/topic, and the compiler's notes transparently document that her stated channel-membership rationale is factually inaccurate per the seed but does not affect the correctness of computed_matches, candidate_population, or negative_referents — appropriately treating this as a writer-side wording defect rather than attempting an unauthorized compiler-side fix. Answer-computation attributes (reaction_type, message_id, messages.channel_id, channels.channel_name) are bare real table.column names computed post-selection, consistent with rules on written/answer attributes. Actor access via conversations.list/members/history, reactions.get, and users.info is realistic given the actor's existing memberships in #engineering, #core-infra, and #random.
